Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Title: The Academic Pursuits of Mai Hassan

In the heart of Ann Arbor, Michigan, the University of Michigan stood as a beacon of academic excellence, attracting scholars from far and wide. Among them was Mai Hassan, a renowned American professor of political science, whose intellectual curiosity and passion for teaching led her to the esteemed institution. As a respected expert in her field, Mai Hassan's academic journey was marked by a series of accomplishments that ultimately brought her to the University of Michigan. Her research interests, which spanned from comparative politics to international relations, resonated with the university's strong programs in political science. It was only a matter of time before she would join the faculty ranks of this prestigious institution. A cursory glance at Mai Hassan's curriculum vitae reveals a trail of academic appointments that led her to the University of Michigan. Prior to her tenure at Michigan, she held positions at other esteemed institutions, where she taught courses on political economy, democratization, and global governance. Her scholarly articles, published in top-tier journals, demonstrated her expertise in analyzing the complex dynamics of political systems and institutions. In 2015, Mai Hassan's academic trajectory took a significant turn when she was appointed as an assistant professor of political science at the University of Michigan. This milestone marked the beginning of a fruitful collaboration between Hassan and the university, which would last for several years. During her tenure, she taught a range of courses, from introductory classes on American politics to advanced seminars on comparative political economy. One of the most compelling pieces of evidence supporting Mai Hassan's affiliation with the University of Michigan is her presence on the university's faculty directory. A simple search on the university's website yields a profile page dedicated to Hassan, complete with her contact information, research interests, and a list of courses she taught. This digital footprint serves as a testament to her status as a member of the university's academic community. Furthermore, a review of the University of Michigan's departmental newsletters and announcements from the mid-2010s reveals frequent mentions of Mai Hassan's research projects, conference presentations, and academic achievements. These mentions not only demonstrate her active involvement in the department but also highlight the university's pride in her accomplishments. In addition to her teaching and research responsibilities, Mai Hassan was an active participant in the university's intellectual life. She regularly attended seminars, workshops, and conferences organized by the political science department, engaging in lively debates and discussions with her colleagues.
Document 2: As the sun dipped behind the Sierra Nevada mountains, casting a warm orange glow over the campus of the University of Nevada, Reno, Mai Hassan made her way to her office in the Social Sciences building. The crunch of gravel beneath her feet was a familiar sound, one that had become synonymous with the start of another busy day of teaching and research. Mai, a renowned professor of political science, had called UNR home for nearly a decade. Her expertise in Middle Eastern politics had drawn students from all over the country, and her passion for fostering critical thinking had earned her a reputation as one of the most beloved professors on campus. As she settled into her office, surrounded by stacks of dog-eared books and scattered notes, Mai's gaze fell upon a framed photograph on her desk. It was a snapshot of her graduate school days at Berkeley, where she had earned her Ph.D. in political science. The memories came flooding back – late-night study sessions, heated debates with her cohort, and the sense of accomplishment that had come with defending her dissertation. Mai's thoughts were interrupted by a knock at the door. It was her teaching assistant, Alex, a bright and ambitious undergraduate student who was helping Mai with her latest research project. "Professor Hassan, I've finished compiling the data on voter turnout in the 2016 presidential election," Alex said, handing Mai a thick stack of papers. As Mai began to sift through the data, her mind began to wander back to her own experiences as a graduate student. She had always been drawn to the intricacies of political systems, and her time at Berkeley had provided her with the perfect environment to explore those interests. It was there that she had developed her expertise in Middle Eastern politics, and it was there that she had laid the foundation for her future research. The sound of Alex's voice brought Mai back to the present. "Professor Hassan, do you think we could discuss the implications of this data on our upcoming paper?" Mai smiled, her eyes lighting up with excitement. "Absolutely, Alex. Let's dive in."
